title: Bidirectional A* in Reykjavík: Find the Fast Route!
description: Watch Bidirectional A* slice through Reykjavík’s street-map graph, meeting in the middle to cut search work. This visualization shows how two informed frontiers coordinate to locate an efficient path faster than a single-direction search.
ig_caption:
❄️🗺️ Reykjavík streets + smart graph search = ⚡

Bidirectional A* runs two simultaneous A* searches—one expanding from the start and one from the goal—using heuristics to stay goal-directed. When the forward and backward frontiers meet, we stitch the optimal route together, often reducing explored nodes compared to classic A* on real street-map graphs. 

Under the hood: each intersection is a node, roads are weighted edges, and the heuristic guides expansion toward the opposite side of the map. That “meet-in-the-middle” strategy is the key to faster convergence on large navigation graphs like those found in real-world city networks. 📍🔧

fb_caption:
🧠🚦 In this reel, Bidirectional A* searches a real street-map graph of Reykjavík (Vesturbær) by expanding from both the start and the goal at the same time. By combining graph theory (nodes/edges/weights) with heuristic-guided search, it often reaches the destination with fewer explored routes than one-way A*.
